ui.aboutDescription: ORBITAL connects planetary maps with astronomical calculations. Explore terrain and cloud patterns, rotate the model and inspect the selected planet’s current position relative to the Sun.
ui.aboutFactText: Appearance is based on surface and atmospheric maps. Each planet’s view includes its sources and credits.
ui.aboutModelText: Sun direction and rotation follow astronomical models. You can freely rotate the viewing camera.
ui.aboutAccessText: Astronomy Engine calculates heliocentric coordinates for the current UTC time, refreshed every minute.
ui.visualNote: Maps based on spacecraft imagery. Positions are date-driven; atmospheric effects are simulated. Models are not shown at a common scale.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.headline: Stillness next to the Sun.
mercury.introduction: A small world with a long memory. Mercury’s craters preserve ancient impacts, while its nearly airless surface faces sunlight without shelter.

first.title: Between heat and cold
first.text: A tenuous exosphere barely retains heat. Sunlit ground becomes intensely hot, while the long night brings deep cold.

second.title: Ice beside the Sun
second.text: Sunlight never reaches the floors of some polar craters. Water ice can survive in their permanent shadows.

third.title: An unexpected rhythm
third.text: Mercury spins three times for every two trips around the Sun. Its solar day is therefore much longer than its year.

mercury.discovery: The closest planet to the Sun shelters ice where dawn never arrives.

venus.name: Venus
venus.headline: Beauty behind a golden veil.
venus.introduction: From Earth, Venus looks like a serene point of light. Beneath its clouds lies a world of volcanic plains, immense pressure and heat with little escape.

first.title: A world beneath clouds
first.text: A dense carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps heat through the greenhouse effect. Venus is hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun.

second.title: The other direction
second.text: Venus slowly rotates opposite to most planets. A single spin takes longer than its trip around the Sun.

third.title: A hidden landscape
third.text: Sulfuric-acid clouds conceal the terrain from ordinary view. Radar reveals mountains, plains and volcanic structures beneath them.

venus.discovery: The hottest planet in the Solar System occupies only its second orbit.

earth.name: Earth
earth.headline: Everything familiar, on one sphere.
earth.introduction: A thin blue edge separates our home from space. Oceans, air and a living surface form an interconnected system that never stands still.

first.title: A world of liquid water
first.text: Oceans cover most of the surface. Water circulates between sea, atmosphere and land, moving heat and sustaining life.

second.title: A moving surface
second.text: Tectonic plates move slowly. Their boundaries build mountains, open ocean trenches and drive volcanic activity.

third.title: An atmosphere in detail
third.text: Cloud systems reveal moving air. This model combines satellite imagery with artistic volume rendering; it is not a precise weather forecast.

earth.discovery: The only world we know where life has become part of a planetary system.

mars.name: Mars
mars.headline: The landscape of a vanished sea.
mars.introduction: Red dust conceals the history of a different Mars. Dry valleys and ancient lake deposits point to a time when water reshaped its surface.

first.title: Traces of missing water
first.text: Today’s atmosphere is too thin for stable exposed liquid water. Channels and minerals preserve evidence of a wetter past.

second.title: An extraordinary scale
second.text: Olympus Mons and the Valles Marineris canyon system show how monumental the terrain of a small world can become.

third.title: A planet of dust
third.text: Winds lift fine dust. Some storms spread over vast areas and change the planet’s appearance from space.

mars.discovery: Beneath the red dust lies evidence of a world once reshaped by water.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.headline: A whole world inside a storm.
jupiter.introduction: Jupiter’s pale zones and dark belts trace a moving atmosphere. Beneath them lies a giant composed mostly of hydrogen and helium.

first.title: No familiar shoreline
first.text: Jupiter has no ordinary solid surface. Pressure rises with depth, gradually changing the properties of its material.

second.title: A storm with a history
second.text: The Great Red Spot is a vast, persistent vortex. Its shape and size change, and observations span centuries.

third.title: A rapid rotation
third.text: Jupiter spins once in roughly ten hours. Its fast rotation accompanies a noticeable flattening at the poles.

jupiter.discovery: The largest planet completes a rotation faster than any of the others.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.headline: An architecture of ice and light.
saturn.introduction: From afar, the rings seem like a single structure. Up close, they are countless separate particles, each following its own orbit around the planet.

first.title: Rings without solid walls
first.text: Ice, rock and dust form a thin, extensive system. The gravity of moons helps sculpt gaps and patterns within the rings.

second.title: The giant beneath
second.text: Saturn is mostly hydrogen and helium. Its cloudy atmosphere conceals deep layers with increasing pressure.

third.title: Neighbouring worlds
third.text: Titan has a dense atmosphere and hydrocarbon lakes. Enceladus ejects water ice from beneath its surface.

saturn.discovery: The apparently solid rings are actually countless independent orbiting particles.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.headline: A world with a different sense of up.
uranus.introduction: A quiet blue disc conceals unusual geometry. Uranus is tilted so far that it appears to roll along its orbit.

first.title: Seasons measured in decades
first.text: The extreme tilt creates prolonged polar days and nights. One orbit takes about 84 Earth years.

second.title: What ‘ice giant’ means
second.text: The term describes deep material rich in water, ammonia and methane. It does not imply a solid, frozen surface.

third.title: A delicate colour
third.text: Atmospheric methane absorbs some red light. A cold atmosphere and a system of faint rings surround the deeper layers.

uranus.discovery: Here, the familiar rhythm of days, nights and seasons takes on a different scale.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.headline: Motion at the edge of darkness.
neptune.introduction: Distant Neptune receives only a fraction of our familiar sunlight. Yet its atmosphere is alive with clouds, powerful winds and changing dark vortices.

first.title: Far from the light
first.text: At this distance, noon is far dimmer than on Earth. A Neptunian year lasts about 165 Earth years.

second.title: A restless atmosphere
second.text: Large storm systems form in the atmosphere. Methane affects the planet’s colour and forms bright, high-altitude clouds.

third.title: Calculation came first
third.text: Neptune was found after calculations explained deviations in Uranus’s orbit. Observers confirmed the predicted planet in 1846.

neptune.discovery: A planet predicted by mathematics before it was found through a telescope.
